title: LayerGroup — Layer Organization and Navigation
description: LayerGroups organize layers into hierarchical categories shown in the left panel. Each group belongs to a site_scope and may have a parent (super_group). Layers are linked to groups via Agrupation join records.

key_fields.name: Display name shown in the sidebar (translated).
key_fields.slug: URL-safe identifier for the group, unique per site_scope.
key_fields.super_group_id: Optional. Foreign key to parent LayerGroup for nesting.
key_fields.layer_group_type: Controls display mode and hierarchy. Supported values in current admin flows: 'group', 'category', 'subcategory', 'subgroup'.
key_fields.category: Optional grouping category label for the group.
key_fields.active: Boolean. Default active state on page load.
key_fields.order: Integer display order within the parent group.
key_fields.icon_class: Optional CSS icon class for the group icon.

linking_layers.description: When creating or updating a layer, pass site_scope_id and layer_group_id. The admin API creates the Agrupation automatically, and the agent passes layer_group_id inside the nested layer payload.

how_to_find_groups: Use get_site_scopes(site_scope_id=...) to list groups for the selected site scope. Prefer that over scraping IDs from the admin UI.
usage_notes: A layer can belong to multiple layer groups (via multiple Agrupation records), but this is uncommon.
If the correct layer group does not exist, create it with create_layer_group or POST /api/admin/layer_groups before assigning the layer.
For a top-level category, omit super_group_id and use layer_group_type='category'.
The super_group_id creates nesting — sub-groups appear nested under their parent in the sidebar.
When layer_group_id is supplied, the admin layer create/update flow links to that explicit group instead of defaulting to 'New uploads'.
